newsitem.title: USA: Infisa SA, Chase, others in $750 mln pact.
newsitem.headline: Infisa SA, Chase, others in $750 mln pact.

text.p: Chile's Infisa SA said Sunday it has an agreement with a four-member investor group to jointly invest about $750 million in financial companies throughout Latin America.
The group will commit $350 million, the privately held company said.

It said its partners include Chase Capital Partners, the private equity investment group of Chase Manhattan Bank, and Natcan Holdings International Ltd, a unit of National Bank of Canada, each of which will invest $75 million.

It said its two other partners are Blackstone Capital Partners II Merchant Banking Fund LP, run by New York's Blackstone Group, and the Dallas-based group of Hicks Muse Tate & First Inc, each of which will invest $100 million.
The goal is to establish the first Latin-American wide financial institution, the company said in a release.
The transaction is the largest of its kind executed in Latin America, said John Anderson, a spokesman for Chase Manhattan Corp.
The first acquisitions of the venture are Banco Conception of Chile and Venezuela's Banco Consolidado. Both acquisitions are subject to regulatory approval, Anderson said.
Infisa, which is controlled by Alvaro Saieh, has a controlling interest in Provida, Chile's largest investment fund, and in two Chilean insurance companies.
Saieh will be chairman of the new entity, which has yet to be named, Infisa said in a release.
